review_candidates.title: Wind Turbine Service Technician - Kilbraur, Scottish Highlands
review_candidates.description: Do you share our passion of renewable energy for a greener and sustainable future? Nordex has an exciting opportunity for the role of Wind Turbine Service Technician based at Kilbraur Windfarm in the Scottish Highlands. Contract Type: Permanent Location: Kilbraur Windfarm, Strath Brora, Scottish Highlands Hours: Our core hours are 37 per week (Monday – Thursday 8am – 4:30pm and Friday 8am till 1pm) with a requirement to work overtime when required. Our Service Technicians are also required to be available for any breakdowns and faults at the weekend, working on-call every 2nd or 3rd weekend (depending on the size of your team). Overtime is paid at time and a half, and you will receive an additional payment for the weekend you are on on-call. As our Service Technicians are required to work overtime and on call there is a requirement for successful candidates to live within a radius of up to 1 hour from the windfarm. How can you make a difference? As a Wind Turbine Service Technician, you will be responsible for the servicing and maintenance of Nordex wind turbines covering turbines at Kilbraur Windfarm in the Scottish Highlands . You will carry out general and specialised work including repairs, troubleshooting and fault-finding activities ensuing our wind turbines continue to achieve a high level of availability. What will you be doing? You will be responsible for Wind Turbine availability, which means physically troubleshooting turbines not performing to capacity on various wind farms, as well as analysing data and other information to be able to create and support implementing action plans that will increase performance in the fleet. Key Responsibilities For This Role Include On site performance analysis and action plan implementation Working closely with Technicians and Back Office staff to perform on the job demonstrations Supporting on site single turbine improvements on problem turbines Providing on site software & hardware updates Supporting on-line and on phone technical support Creating reports on turbine or turbine components Parameter disabling and alarm change handling when necessary What are we looking for? The ideal candidate will have experience of working in the Mechanical / Electrical industry and be able to demonstrate knowledge of reading electrical, hydraulic and mechanical diagrams. You will be Mechanical or Electrical trained through time-served or a technical college qualification which should be at least NVQ Level 3 or equivalent. You will be able to demonstrate you can identify and define problems, extract crucial information from technical data, and develop workable solutions to problems Other essential skills and behaviours required for this role include: The ability to adapt to an environment of continuous change and different challenges A positive attitude with a willingness to learn, lead and continuously improve Computer literate and confident in using MS office packages, in house databases and workload management systems This role involves working at heights, up to 140m. You will need to be fit and health and pass a working at height test. You will be required to travel on an occasional basis which includes nights away from home A full UK / EU Driving Licence is required for this role. What we can offer you? Time Off Our teams receive 33 days annual leave including bank holidays. After two years continual service you will be entitled to an additional day‘s holiday per annum (Maximum 5 days). You will also an extra day off for your birthday. In addition we also offer our employees the opportunity to purchase up to 5 day of additional annual leave every year. Benefits Health & Wellbeing - The Health and Wellbeing of our employees is incredibly important, which is why we have different benefits for our employees including: Employee Assistance Programme (offering therapy sessions) Bike2Work Scheme Paid Eye tests & contribution towards Glasses Company Sick pay scheme The option to purchase Private Healthcare Volunteering - All our employees can use 2 paid working days per calendar year to carry out volunteering activities in your local community. Family friendly - Our family friendly policies include, Enhanced Maternity, Paternity and Adoption Leave. Compassionate Leave, and Life Insurance. Memberships - Nordex will reimburse the cost of one annual professional subscription fee to one professional institution relevant to your work. Recruitment Process The closing date for this role is Friday 30th October 2026 , however, please be aware that this role could close early if we receive an overwhelming response. The first stage of the recruitment process requires you to submit your CV via the Apply Now button. The recruitment team will then review your application and be in touch to confirm if you have been successful in reaching the next stage of the process. We appreciate all the applications we receive and will be in touch with you as soon as we can, so please watch out for our emails or phone calls (which maybe from a withheld number) Nordex Values, Diversity & Inclusion Here at Nordex we interact with a variety of people and cultures. Our values of Integrity, Respect, Colleagueship, and Ownership are the unifying force for all departments and regions around the world, these are the standards we walk by. Our mission is to offer cutting edge, reliable products, and services, generating value for our customers and stakeholders …. All whilst protecting the environment. Join the #TEAMNORDEX and shape the future of energy with us.

review_candidates.title: Vice-présidente ou vice-président associé aux risques et contrôles
review_candidates.description: Entreprise: CCAV Catégories d’emplois: Poste permanent à temps plein Modèle de travail: Hybride (2 jours au bureau) Langue: Le ou la titulaire de ce poste travaille en anglais. Renseignements supplémentaires : Ce(s) poste(s) est/sont actuellement vacant. L’opportunité : Nous sommes une coopérative canadienne de services financiers de premier plan engagée à promouvoir activement une société durable et résiliente, et notre équipe est essentielle au succès de cette stratégie. C’est pourquoi nos gens sont notre priorité. Nous offrons une culture d’entreprise vivante et des occasions de perfectionnement qui permettent à notre équipe d’exploiter tout son potentiel et de concrétiser notre raison d’être. Et le meilleur : vous travaillerez avec des personnes qui se soucient vraiment de vous, de notre clientèle et de nos collectivités. En qualité de vice-présidente ou vice-président associé aux risques et contrôles, vous dirigez la fonction des risques et des contrôles de CCAV, en assurant une surveillance indépendante afin de renforcer la gestion des risques, les mesures de contrôle internes, la conformité et la prévention de la fraude. Vous supervisez les programmes de certification et de conformité de l’entreprise, les tests des contrôles et la production de rapports, le plan de continuité des activités (PCA), la gestion des risques de l’entreprise (GRE), la gestion du risque lié à la modélisation et aux tiers, ainsi que la surveillance des pratiques commerciales. La personne retenue sera chargée de promouvoir une solide culture de gestion des risques, d’améliorer les cadres de gouvernance et les mesures de contrôle, de garantir la conformité aux exigences légales et réglementaires et de fournir des rapports stratégiques sur les risques et des analyses à la haute direction. Comment vous créez un impact : Diriger et faire évoluer la première ligne de défense de la fonction des risques et des contrôles de CCAV, notamment en ce qui concerne la structure de l’équipe, la planification des capacités, le perfectionnement des talents et la gestion du rendement. Agir à titre de responsable de la première ligne de défense pour les examens réglementaires, les audits internes, les activités de surveillance de la deuxième ligne de défense et les évaluations menées par des tiers, en veillant à la mise en œuvre des mesures correctives et de la résolution en temps opportun. Fournir à la haute direction des rapports et des analyses sur les activités liées aux risques, aux mesures de contrôle, aux audits et à la conformité, en mettant en lumière les principales tendances, les résultats et les possibilités d’amélioration. Veiller à ce que les évaluations des risques orientent les priorités en matière de surveillance, d’audit, de production de rapports et de mesures correctives à l’échelle de l’entreprise. Superviser le programme de gestion du risque de modélisation et veiller au respect constant des lignes directrices du BSIF. Diriger les programmes de gestion du risque lié aux tiers et de surveillance des pratiques commerciales, notamment en matière de gouvernance, de suivi et de gestion des cas d’acheminement à un niveau supérieur. Travailler en étroite collaboration avec les équipes responsables de la conformité, des audits internes et de la gestion des risques de l’entreprise (deuxième ligne de défense) afin de renforcer l’identification, la prise en charge et l’atténuation des risques. Favoriser une culture axée sur la performance, la collaboration et la gestion des risques grâce à l’accompagnement, au mentorat et au perfectionnement en leadership. Pour joindre notre équipe : Baccalauréat en administration des affaires, en finance, en science actuarielle, en statistique, en gestion des risques ou dans un domaine connexe. Titres de CPA, FICA, CERA, CIA, PAA ou FPAA, un atout. Plus de 10 ans d’expérience dans des postes de direction à responsabilité croissante dans le secteur de l’assurance. Expérience dans les domaines des audits, de l’assurance, de la gestion des risques de l’entreprise ou de la gouvernance, un atout. Excellente compréhension des opérations d’assurance, des fonctions opérationnelles de première ligne et du modèle des trois lignes de défense. Expertise en matière de gestion des risques de l’entreprise (GRE), de risques et de cadres de contrôle, de continuité des activités et de méthodologies de gestion des risques. Connaissance des outils intégrés d’analytique avancée, des capacités en matière de données et de leur application aux activités liées aux risques et aux mesures de contrôle. Comment vous brillez : Vous mettez en œuvre de nouvelles stratégies en vue de saisir les occasions qui se présentent et dirigez la mise en œuvre du changement organisationnel. Vous tenez compte de données complexes pour trouver des solutions ou résoudre des problèmes et faites preuve d’esprit stratégique pour ajuster les plans d’affaires. Vous favorisez l’innovation et l’amélioration continue axées sur l’expérience client. Vous créez une culture axée sur la performance en veillant à ce que le travail de votre équipe concorde avec les objectifs organisationnels et transmettez efficacement les messages avec un sentiment de représentation positive. Vous formez les autres afin de s’assurer qu’ils répondent aux besoins en évolution de l’entreprise et établissez des relations efficaces en vue d’atteindre les principaux objectifs de l’entreprise. Ce que vous devez savoir : Si votre candidature est retenue, nous procéderons à la vérification de votre solvabilité et de vos antécédents judiciaires comme condition d’embauche. Comment vous en bénéficiez : Occasions de formation et de perfectionnement vous permettant de bâtir votre carrière. Horaire de travail flexible et congés rémunérés pour subvenir à vos besoins et à ceux de votre famille. Approche globale à l’égard de votre bien-être, programmes de santé physique et mentale et culture solidaire en milieu de travail. Journées de bénévolat rémunérées pour redonner à votre collectivité. En plus de nos salaires concurrentiels et de nos programmes incitatifs, les employées et employés admissibles bénéficient également d’un programme de rémunération globale complet, y compris des régimes d’épargne-retraite collectifs et une assurance collective (p. ex., assurance soins médicaux, mieux-être, soins dentaires, invalidité et vie), du soutien en santé mentale et un programme d’aide aux employés et employées. Échelle salariale de 142,526.00 $ à 237,544.00 $ . Le montant du salaire de la candidate ou du candidat retenu est déterminé par Co-operators, à sa discrétion, et varie en fonction de plusieurs critères, notamment : les conditions du marché local, la région géographique et les facteurs pertinents liés au poste, comme les connaissances, les compétences, les aptitudes, l’expérience et la formation. Les employées et employés peuvent également avoir la possibilité de participer à des programmes incitatifs et de gagner une rémunération supplémentaire en fonction de leur rendement individuel ou de celui de l’entreprise, ou d’autres mesures commerciales.

review_candidates.description: Role: Senior Compiler Engineer About Tensordyne Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming our world. It can perform cognitive functions that previously only humans could do, such as perceiving interactions across different modalities and environments - with the ability to quickly learn and then solve complex problems. Tensordyne is an AI system solution company that builds very high-performance, low-power generative AI inference systems. Our mission, through the creation of custom silicon, hardware and software, is to enable multimodal Generative AI inference acceleration at scale, with safe, sustainable, high-performance systems for our hyperscaler and neocloud data center customers. We are at the leading edge of advancing the latest research and product improvements for generative Al inference solutions that will make Al even more advantageous for compelling new generative AI applications. Tensordyne is a well funded, fast-paced startup company with headquarters in both Sunnyvale, CA, and Munich, Germany. We also have many talented team members working remotely across North America and Europe. We take care of our people and their families with comprehensive benefits, competitive compensation, flexible spending options, and recognition programs, because building category-defining technology starts with a healthy, supported team. Come join us as we shape the future of multimodal generative artificial intelligence! About the Role The compiler decides whether our inference silicon runs at 30% utilization or 90% or more. That's the job. Together with our team, you'll build the backend that turns AI workloads into microcode for Tensordyne hardware - Napier today and the silicon that follows. This is a clean-slate compiler effort targeting a genuinely unusual architecture. You'll have the opportunity to work on fundamental parts of the compiler. The users are changing, too. Increasingly, model mapping and optimization will be done by agents as well as engineers. A compiler designed primarily for humans tends to optimize for escape hatches and manual control. A compiler designed to work effectively with agents needs transparent cost models, structured feedback, machine-readable diagnostics, and fast closed-loop iteration. We need both in the same stack and very few teams are building for this interaction today. What You'll Do Contribute to backend compilation end to end: lowering, instruction scheduling, register and resource allocation, and microcode generation. Consider the memory hierarchy: SRAM residency, HBM traffic, DMA orchestration, layout, rematerialization, and data movement. The goal is simple: keep the machine compute-bound rather than waiting on memory. Develop tiling, fusion, and software-pipelining strategies that close the gap between theoretical and achieved throughput. Design compiler interfaces that work for both agents and engineers: structured IR access, machine-readable diagnostics, searchable tuning spaces, and actionable performance feedback. Solve problems conventional batch compilers often avoid: dynamic shapes, compile latency, KV-cache management, and the different optimization objectives of time-to-first-token (TTFT) versus steady-state throughput. Build cost models that predict performance on silicon that doesn't exist yet, then continuously calibrate those models against real hardware. Feed compiler learnings back into ISA and microarchitecture requirements for the next generation of silicon. What We're Looking For Production compiler experience in code generation, optimization, or graph mapping. Tell us what you shipped and what it achieved, not how many years you've been doing it. Experience with MLIR and/or LLVM , with meaningful contributions to an active compiler stack such as LLVM, MLIR, TVM, IREE, XLA, Triton, Inductor, or an equivalent internal system. Strong modern C++ skills and a disciplined approach to testing and correctness. Rust experience is a plus. Experience targeting custom accelerators or non-standard ISAs. You should be comfortable reading a microarchitecture specification, understanding its implications, and arguing with its assumptions when the compiler says they don't hold. Strong performance intuition: memory hierarchy, data movement, parallelism, synchronization, occupancy, and the factors that determine whether theoretical hardware throughput becomes real throughput. A co-design mindset. Compiler, kernels, runtime, ISA, and silicon are one system. You'll cross those boundaries whenever that's where the performance opportunity is. What Stands Out Defensible opinions about what today's ML compilers get wrong and evidence behind them. Work on autotuning, auto-scheduling, or polyhedral compilation. Serious hands-on experience using agents in compiler, kernel-generation, or optimization loops. CUDA/Triton expertise, particularly with the CUTLASS or NCCL ecosystems. Experience with VLIW, systolic, dataflow, or other unconventional architectures. Open-source compiler contributions we can read and discuss. Tensordyne is an equal opportunity employer. review_candidates.description: Company Overview Pattern Energy is a leading renewable energy company that develops, constructs, owns, and operates high-quality wind and solar generation, transmission, and energy storage facilities. Our mission is to transition the world to renewable energy through the sustainable development and responsible operation of facilities with respect for the environment, communities, and cultures where we have a presence. Our approach begins and ends with establishing trust, accountability, and transparency. Our company values of creative spirit, pride of ownership, follow-through, and a team-first attitude drive us to pursue our mission every day. Our culture supports our values by fostering innovative and critical thinking and a deep belief in living up to our promises. Headquartered in the United States, Pattern has a global portfolio of more than 46 power facilities and transmission assets, serving various customers that provide low-cost clean energy to millions of consumers. Responsibilities Job Purpose The Senior Project Controller is responsible for leading project controls, financial oversight, forecasting, and financial performance reporting for large-scale renewable energy capital projects and programs. This role ensures effective cost management, cash flow forecasting, and compliance with financial-related financing and governance requirements across the project lifecycle. The position works closely with project management, engineering, construction, procurement, finance, and executive leadership to support successful delivery of capital renewable energy projects. Key Accountabilities The key responsibilities will include as a minimum the following: Oversee Engineering, Procurement and Construction ("EPC"), construction, supplier, and consulting agreements to ensure compliance with financial requirements, budget alignment, and effective cost control across capital projects. Ability to work within a dynamic multiple discipline working environment and support in the negotiation and development of EPC agreements, supplier agreements and change management processes. Manage commitments, change orders, invoices, and payment applications while supporting claims management and accurate project cost reporting. Lead the maintenance of project controls systems and cost reporting to support accurate tracking of project performance and financial outcomes. Develop executive-level reports and dashboards while driving continuous improvement in project controls governance, reporting standards, and data integrity. Support project financing activities including financial close requirements, lender reporting, funding requests, and cash flow tracking, for renewable energy capital projects. Coordinate with multiple stakeholders to support financial compliance and capital forecasting. Lead project controls activities for renewable energy capital projects including cost control, budgeting, forecasting, and reporting. Establish and maintain project budgets, cost baselines, cost control, cash flow forecasts, and contingency tracking throughout the project life cycle. Perform variance analyses and provide recommendations to mitigate cost and project delivery risks throughout the project lifecycle, supporting risk management activities as required. Advanced understanding of project controls capability and maturity assessments. Strong understanding and ability to analyze earned value management (EVM) and key performance indicator (KPI) performance. Good understanding of financial-related construction contract concepts, language, requirements and terms. Experience working on major capital projects/programs with familiarity with activities, stage gate process and management. Able to lead and guide best practice solutions in the development of cost controls and cost-related performance processes and digital solutions. Ability to mentor and develop project controls personnel while promoting best practices and technical competency development. Strong communication skills and ability to liaise across multidisciplinary teams, including Business Development, Finance, Accounting, Contracts Management, Project Management groups and external counterparties. Experience managing project controls activities across multiple projects or large capital programs within a construction and procurement environment. Support cost-related project governance reviews/audits, stage gate approvals, and executive decision-making processes throughout the project lifecycle. Experience/Qualifications/Education Qualifications Educational Experience 5–10 years of construction and/or procurement project controls experience within major capital and infrastructure projects. Degree qualification or equivalent in Construction Management, Engineering, Finance, Quantity Surveying, Project Management or related field. Additional Requirements Excellent analytical and cost control skills. Experience within renewable energy sectors is highly desirable. Strong organizational, analytical, and communication skills with excellent attention to detail. Strong and proven understanding of project controls principles, including cost control, forecasting, earned value management (EVM), and project performance reporting. Technical Skills Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and MS Office suite. Experience with ERP and project management systems (e.g., Oracle, Power BI, D365, InEight, Procure, SAP) preferred. The expected starting pay range for this role is $103,000 - $138,000 USD. This range is an estimate and base pay may be above or below the ranges based on several factors including but not limited to location, work experience, certifications, and education. In addition to base pay, Pattern’s compensation program includes a bonus structure for full-time employees of all levels. We also provide a comprehensive benefits package which includes medical, dental, vision, short and long-term disability, life insurance, voluntary benefits, family care benefits, employee assistance program, paid time off and bonding leave, paid holidays, 401(k)/RRSP retirement savings plan with employer contribution, and employee referral bonuses. Pattern Energy Group is an Equal Opportunity Employer.
